claims.text: MLIP-driven molecular dynamics can reliably predict melting temperatures of high-melting refractory materials.
MLIP-driven molecular dynamics can reliably predict entropy of fusion.
MLIP-driven molecular dynamics can reliably predict enthalpy of fusion.
MLIP-driven molecular dynamics can reliably predict volume change at the melting point.
MLIP-driven simulations dramatically reduce computational cost relative to full ab initio DFT approaches.
An MLIP trained on a representative DFT dataset can be used to calculate the free-energy difference between solid and liquid phases.
Coexistence simulations or thermodynamic integration can be used with an MLIP to determine melting phase boundaries.
A suitable ML potential accurately captures atomistic interactions, including anharmonic effects.
Accurate atomistic interactions allow the ML potential to describe both solid and liquid phases.
DFT-trained MLIPs can emulate ab initio accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost.
The reduced cost of MLIPs enables high-throughput evaluation of phase free energies.
Comparing solid and liquid free-energy curves under comparable conditions enables prediction of melting properties.
MLIP-based predictions are expected to agree with DFT predictions within approximately ±10%.
Accuracy within approximately ±10% would make MLIP simulations suitable for high-throughput screening of refractory materials.
Ab initio DFT free-energy approaches are accurate for calculating melting properties.
Ab initio DFT free-energy approaches are computationally prohibitive for high-throughput calculations.
MLIP accuracy depends on the quality and representativeness of its training data.
Additional validation may be necessary for novel refractory chemistries, strong anharmonicity, or systems outside the MLIP training domain.
The exact MLIP error margin is uncertain across diverse refractory systems.
A systematic discrepancy greater than ±10% relative to full DFT results is defined as falsifying the proposed accuracy claim.
